improvements_suggested: Repair the milestone->commit windowing in the timing-data collector so the retro receives the milestone's actual experiment commits, and prove it end-to-end on a live retro (it must report the real .372 experiment range, not 0).

Add a detector-independent fallback: glob results/experiment_*.json (or git log) for commits since the activation SHA, plus a loud self-check that FAILS when the count is 0 but on-disk artifacts/changelog entries for the milestone exist, so a future retro cannot silently run on empty input.

top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Fix the milestone-scoped commit detector and validate it end-to-end on a live retro (report the real exp range, not 0) — this is the recurring root cause across 8 milestones.
Ship a detector-independent glob/git fallback plus a zero-but-artifacts-present self-check that fails loudly, so retros never again run on a false-zero.
Verify-or-revert the prior 'detector fixed' claim rather than carrying it forward unverified for another milestone.
meta_reflection: For the 8th time the operational retro received a false-zero timing block while the milestone actually shipped real work (per the on-disk changelog), so the recurring lesson is observability, not efficiency: there is no experiment wall-clock to reclaim (the experiments ran fine), only an attribution gap that makes the retro honest-but-empty. The highest-leverage fix is making the detector either correct or loudly self-failing on zero-with-artifacts. Per the anti-hallucination guard the locked numeric fields stay 0 (the authoritative block) and no durations/metrics are invented; the experiment range is sourced with provenance from ops/changelog.md read this turn and recorded only in the research-log narrative.
